# VERDICT 2 ? MOBILE PLAN AMENDMENT: **NEEDS REVISION** (2 blocking, 6 major)

No native app exists in this tree ? no `apps/mobile`, `app.json`, `eas.json` or Expo dependency. This is a plan amendment only, and I am not claiming otherwise.

## BLOCKING

- **B1 ? no repository/build topology for `apps/mobile`.** `PLAN.md:217` says "Add one Expo/React Native app in apps/mobile, retaining the Next.js site in place" and stops there. The Next.js app lives at the **repo root** (`package.json`, `src/`, `tsconfig` all at root) and `package.json` has **no `workspaces` key** (verified). The plan never decides whether mobile gets its own package.json and lockfile, whether npm workspaces are adopted, or how `npm ci` from the existing root lockfile (`CLAUDE.md`, Local work) stays valid. Both branches have real consequences: adopting workspaces rewrites the root lockfile and changes what Railway installs on every web deploy; not adopting them means a second independent lockfile with no dedupe. This *is* the smallest-maintainable-architecture question and it is unanswered.
- **B2 ? "share suitable pure logic" has no mechanism.** `PLAN.md:217`. With web at the root and mobile at `apps/mobile`, cross-boundary TypeScript sharing needs either a workspace package or imports outside the Metro project root, and Metro will not resolve parent-directory or symlinked sources without explicit `watchFolders` + `resolver.nodeModulesPaths` config. As written this degrades into copy-paste duplication (contradicting "one server entitlement model" / one contract) or an unplanned `packages/shared` refactor mid-P01. Decide now: a shared workspace package, or explicitly "no shared code, mobile is an HTTP client only".
